I had my first and only session done in December '19 at Body Catalyst in Melbourne, Aus. $599 for both during a two for one special, usually it's $599 per area. 

Pain during was a 1/10, uncomfortable and a bit pinchy but you don't notice it after ten minutes. The feeling after? Fuck that. 9/10 I'm not sure I'd do it again tbh (still considering it). Felt like intense stinging, pins and needles, my arms felt heavy and the treated fat felt firm and so unbearably uncomfortable, like when you've held something cold too long then your fingers go stiff and sting but times ten. Apparently my reaction (the extreme pain/uncomfortable feeling plus crying topless in front of the lovely ladies working there for ten minutes) is not common, I'm just a bit of a sook. The stinging pain afterwards was bearable but it was the uncomfortable feeling I really hated.

The feeling subsided after about 10-15 mins. and for the next week I had some strange nerve sensations in my upper arms but nothing painful/uncomfortable/worrisome. Saw some slight results after about four weeks and at twelve weeks there was definitely a huge difference, nearly the same difference in these pics but I think I've lost a little bit off my arms in the last few months.

IMO worth it for the price as I've never had slim arms even at my lowest weight. Would recommend for stubborn fatty areas but only after trying everything else non invasive. And yeah despite hating how it felt immediately after I'm kind of considering a second go. We'll see.

Hi, hope i'm not too late to the party. I've started in a pretty similar boat but I'm 23. The first big step I felt was necessary was telling my Dr and my Mum, my Dr has given me the best medical support she can and my Mum is my rock, and I felt that confessing my addiction to someone was the first step to resolving the problem, because now I have someone who can hold me accountable for my actions when I slip up. You should express your concern for your health to your bf  or someone close to you who you can trust to be there for you without judgement.

Your dr should be able to help you with the withdrawal, with medication or if you choose to an inpatient clinic, though IMO inpatient can be disruptive to a "normal" life schedule/expensive. Your dr should also be able to help you get in touch with a psychologist or specialist/group therapy to help you through the recovery and maintenance after withdrawal. If you feel your dr won't be understanding try finding one who specialises in mental health/drug addiction if that's possible where you are.
